definition: Repentant means feeling and showing sincere regret for wrongdoing.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word repentant. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know repentant should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Repentant at last, the prankster spent his Saturday scrubbing every locker he had glitter-bombed.
Embarrassed is far milder than repentant — the surface flush of being caught, cheeks hot, wishing the moment away, with none of the sincere regret that repentant requires.
Sorry goes further than embarrassed — the regret is real and gets said — but it stops short of repentant, which carries that regret into visible amends.

Remorseful means full of the gnawing feeling of regret, whether or not anyone ever sees it — the guilt can stay hidden for years. Repentant demands both halves: the regret must be felt and shown, in apology, amends, or visibly changed conduct.

Apologetic means saying sorry, and the sorry can run no deeper than good manners — people are apologetic about a missed call or a bumped elbow. Repentant is far heavier: sincere regret for a real wrong, displayed and paid for, never just a courteous phrase in passing.

In his first year on the paper, Tomas Rivera invented a quotation and attached it to a councilwoman who had refused his calls.
A printed correction alone would have satisfied the editors.
Tomas went further: he asked to run it under his own byline, naming what he had done and why it was wrong.
Then he drove to the councilwoman's office and apologized in person, without excuses, and offered to publish her full statement unedited.
For the next year he volunteered for the fact-checking desk, the least glamorous job in the newsroom, checking other reporters' quotations line by line.
His editor said later that plenty of reporters are sorry when they're caught; a repentant one, she said, rebuilds the thing he broke.
